title: Rama passes the night on the banks of Tamasa river
introduction: Having reached the banks of Tamasa river and thinking of the plight of the people of Ayodhya, Rama passes the night on the banks of Tamasa river. Waking up in the meantime, Rama instructs the charioteer to drive the chariot in such a way as to elude the citizens and lead them to think that the chariot had turned back towards Ayodhya instead of proceeding towards the forest. He then ascends the chariot along with Sita and Lakshmana and went ahead to the forest.
closing: इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये अयोध्य काण्डे ष्ट्चत्वारिंशः सर्गः
Thus completes the 46th chapter of Ayodhya Kanda in the glorious Ramayana of Valmiki, the work of a sage and the oldest epic.

verses.devanagari:
ततः तु तमसा तीरम् रम्यम् आश्रित्य राघवः |
सीताम् उद्वीक्ष्य सौमित्रिम् इदम् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
tataḥ tu tamasā tīram ramyam āśritya rāghavaḥ |
sītām udvīkṣya saumitrim idam vacanam abravīt
verses.translation: Then Rama taking his position at the banks of Tamasa river and looking at Sita, spoke to Lakshmana as follows :

glosses.meaning: at the banks of Tamasa river

verses.devanagari:
इयम् अद्य निशा पूर्वा सौमित्रे प्रस्थिता वनम् |
वन वासस्य भद्रम् ते स न उत्कण्ठितुम् अर्हसि
verses.iast:
iyam adya niśā pūrvā saumitre prasthitā vanam |
vana vāsasya bhadram te sa na utkaṇṭhitum arhasi
verses.translation: "Oh, Lakshmana! We have been sent to the forest. Today is the first night of our residence in the forest .You ought not feel anxious. May all be well with you!"

glosses.meaning: of residence in the forest . saH = You as such

verses.devanagari:
पश्य शून्यानि अरण्यानि रुदन्ति इव समन्ततः |
यथा निलयम् आयद्भिर् निलीनानि मृग द्विजैः
verses.iast:
paśya śūnyāni araṇyāni rudanti iva samantataḥ |
yathā nilayam āyadbhir nilīnāni mṛga dvijaiḥ
verses.translation: "Look here: As the animals and birds are returning to their respective abodes seeking for shelter, the desolate woods seem to be crying from all sides"

glosses.meaning: look here: mR^iga dvijaiH = animals and birds

verses.devanagari:
अद्य अयोध्या तु नगरी राज धानी पितुर् मम |
सस्त्री पुंसा गतान् अस्मान् शोचिष्यति न संशयः
verses.iast:
adya ayodhyā tu nagarī rāja dhānī pitur mama |
sastrī puṃsā gatān asmān śociṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
verses.translation: "Now, the city of Ayodhya the capital of my father with its men and women will lament about us that have departed (to the forest). There is no doubt"

glosses.meaning: that have departed. Na = There is no

verses.devanagari:
अनुरक्ता हि मनुजा राजानम् बहुभिर्गुणैः |
त्वाम् च माम् च नरव्याघ्र शत्रघ्नभरतौ तथा
verses.iast:
anuraktā hi manujā rājānam bahubhirguṇaiḥ |
tvām ca mām ca naravyāghra śatraghnabharatau tathā
verses.translation: "Oh, tiger among men! The citizens (of Ayodhya) are indeed having affection to the king no less than to you and myself, as also to Bharata and Satrughna, for many of our virtues."

verses.devanagari:
पितरम् चानुशोचामि मातरम् च यशस्विनीम् |
अपि वानौध भवेताम् तु रुदन्तौ तावभीक्ष्णशः
verses.iast:
pitaram cānuśocāmi mātaram ca yaśasvinīm |
api vānaudha bhavetām tu rudantau tāvabhīkśṇaśaḥ
verses.translation: "I feel repented for my father and my illustrious mother. I fear whether they will become even blind, by weeping incessantly."

glosses.meaning: who is illustrious. tou apivaa bhavetaam = Will they become even

verses.devanagari:
भरतः खलु धर्म आत्मा पितरम् मातरम् च मे |
धर्म अर्थ काम सहितैः वाक्यैः आश्वासयिष्यति
verses.iast:
bharataḥ khalu dharma ātmā pitaram mātaram ca me |
dharma artha kāma sahitaiḥ vākyaiḥ āśvāsayiṣyati
verses.translation: "Bharata, the virtuous man, can indeed console my father and mother by his kind words."

verses.devanagari:
भरतस्य आनृशंसत्वम् संचिन्त्य अहम् पुनः पुनः |
न अनुशोचामि पितरम् मातरम् च अपि लक्ष्मण
verses.iast:
bharatasya ānṛśaṃsatvam saṃcintya aham punaḥ punaḥ |
na anuśocāmi pitaram mātaram ca api lakṣmaṇa
verses.translation: "Oh,Lakshmana! Thinking of Bharata's kindness again and again, I do not grieve for our father and mother"

verses.devanagari:
त्वया कार्यम् नर व्याघ्र माम् अनुव्रजता कृतम् |
अन्वेष्टव्या हि वैदेह्या रक्षण अर्थे सहायता
verses.iast:
tvayā kāryam nara vyāghra mām anuvrajatā kṛtam |
anveṣṭavyā hi vaidehyā rakṣaṇa arthe sahāyatā
verses.translation: "Oh, Lakshmana, tiger among men! You have done well by accompanying me, as otherwise, a help would have to be sought for by me for protecting Seetha"

verses.devanagari:
अद्भिर् एव तु सौमित्रे वत्स्याम्य् अद्य निशाम् इमाम् |
एतद्द् हि रोचते मह्यम् वन्ये अपि विविधे सति
verses.iast:
adbhir eva tu saumitre vatsyāmy adya niśām imām |
etadd hi rocate mahyam vanye api vividhe sati
verses.translation: " Oh, Lakshmana! I shall live on water alone tonight. Though there are various kinds of wild fruits and roots, this is indeed a liking for me"

glosses.meaning: with water alone. vanye = Wild fruits and roots

verses.devanagari:
एवम् उक्त्वा तु सौमित्रम् सुमन्त्रम् अपि राघवः |
अप्रमत्तः त्वम् अश्वेषु भव सौम्य इति उवाच ह
verses.iast:
evam uktvā tu saumitram sumantram api rāghavaḥ |
apramattaḥ tvam aśveṣu bhava saumya iti uvāca ha
verses.translation: Thus telling Lakshmana, Rama spoke also to Sumantra as follows: "Oh, gentle man! Attend to the horses carefully."

verses.devanagari:
सो अश्वान् सुमन्त्रः सम्यम्य सूर्ये अस्तम् समुपागते |
प्रभूत यवसान् कृत्वा बभूव प्रत्यनन्तरः
verses.iast:
so aśvān sumantraḥ samyamya sūrye astam samupāgate |
prabhūta yavasān kṛtvā babhūva pratyanantaraḥ
verses.translation: The sun having completely set, Sumantra tied up the horses, supplied them with abundant grass and immediately stood nearest (to Rama).

glosses.meaning: them to have more grass(to eat)

verses.devanagari:
उपास्यतु शिवाम् संध्याम् दृष्ट्वा रात्रिम् उपस्थिताम् |
रामस्य शयनम् चक्रे सूतः सौमित्रिणा सह
verses.iast:
upāsyatu śivām saṃdhyām dṛṣṭvā rātrim upasthitām |
rāmasya śayanam cakre sūtaḥ saumitriṇā saha
verses.translation: Having worshipped the beautiful evening twilight and having seen the night come nearer, Sumantra along with Lakshmana made the bed for Rama.

verses.devanagari:
ताम् शय्याम् तमसा तीरे वीक्ष्य वृक्ष दलैः कृताम् |
रामः सौमित्रिणाम् सार्धम् सभार्यः सम्विवेश ह
verses.iast:
tām śayyām tamasā tīre vīkṣya vṛkṣa dalaiḥ kṛtām |
rāmaḥ saumitriṇām sārdham sabhāryaḥ samviveśa ha
verses.translation: Seeing that bed made of leaves of a tree on the bank of Tamasa river with the help of Lakshmana, Rama along with his wife laid down on it.

glosses.meaning: on the bank of Tamasa river

verses.devanagari:
सभार्यम् सम्प्रसुप्तम् तम् भ्रातरम् वीक्ष्य लक्ष्मणः |
कथयाम् आस सूताय रामस्य विविधान् गुणान्
verses.iast:
sabhāryam samprasuptam tam bhrātaram vīkṣya lakṣmaṇaḥ |
kathayām āsa sūtāya rāmasya vividhān guṇān
verses.translation: Seeing that brother sleeping along with his wife, Lakshmana narrated Rama's various virtues to Sumantra.

verses.devanagari:
जाग्रतः हि एव ताम् रात्रिम् सौमित्रेर् उदितः रविः |
सूतस्य तमसा तीरे रामस्य ब्रुवतः गुणान्
verses.iast:
jāgrataḥ hi eva tām rātrim saumitrer uditaḥ raviḥ |
sūtasya tamasā tīre rāmasya bruvataḥ guṇān
verses.translation: WhileLakshmana was thus recounting Rama's excellences to Sumantra, keeping awake that whole night at the bank of Tamasa river, the sun rose.

glosses.meaning: at the bank of Tamasa river

verses.devanagari:
गो कुल आकुल तीरायाः तमसायाः विदूरतः |
अवसत् तत्र ताम् रात्रिम् रामः प्रकृतिभिः सह
verses.iast:
go kula ākula tīrāyāḥ tamasāyāḥ vidūrataḥ |
avasat tatra tām rātrim rāmaḥ prakṛtibhiḥ saha
verses.translation: At a good distance from Tamasa river, whose banks were crowded with herds of cows, Rama passed that night there with the citizens.

glosses.meaning: whose banks were crowded with herds of cows

verses.devanagari:
उत्थाय तु महा तेजाः प्रकृतीस् ता निशाम्य च |
अब्रवीद् भ्रातरम् रामः लक्ष्मणम् पुण्य लक्षणम्
verses.iast:
utthāya tu mahā tejāḥ prakṛtīs tā niśāmya ca |
abravīd bhrātaram rāmaḥ lakṣmaṇam puṇya lakṣaṇam
verses.translation: Getting up from the bed and seeing those citizens, Rama with an extraordinary splendor, spoke to his brother, Lakshmana who was endowed with auspicious bodily marks:

glosses.meaning: who was endowed with auspicious bodily marks:

verses.devanagari:
अस्मद् व्यपेक्षान् सौमित्रे निरपेक्षान् गृहेष्व् अपि |
वृक्ष मूलेषु संसुप्तान् पश्य लक्ष्मण साम्प्रतम्
verses.iast:
asmad vyapekṣān saumitre nirapekṣān gṛheṣv api |
vṛkṣa mūleṣu saṃsuptān paśya lakṣmaṇa sāmpratam
verses.translation: "Observe, Oh Lakshmana, the citizens full of longing for us, unmindful even of their homes, sleeping together at the roots of trees, Oh, the son of Sumitra!"

glosses.meaning: (the citizens) full of longing for us

verses.devanagari:
यथा एते नियमम् पौराः कुर्वन्ति अस्मन् निवर्तने |
अपि प्राणान् असिष्यन्ति न तु त्यक्ष्यन्ति निश्चयम्
verses.iast:
yathā ete niyamam paurāḥ kurvanti asman nivartane |
api prāṇān asiṣyanti na tu tyakṣyanti niścayam
verses.translation: "From the way in which these citizens are making coercion to take us back (to Ayodhya), it seems they will even lay down their lives, but in no case would give up their resolve"

verses.devanagari:
यावद् एव तु संसुप्ताः तावद् एव वयम् लघु |
रथम् आरुह्य गच्चामः पन्थानम् अकुतः भयम्
verses.iast:
yāvad eva tu saṃsuptāḥ tāvad eva vayam laghu |
ratham āruhya gaccāmaḥ panthānam akutaḥ bhayam
verses.translation: "Till which time the citizens are asleep, within that time, let us quickly mount the chariot and take a route which has no fear from any quarter"

glosses.meaning: which has no fear from any quarter."

verses.devanagari:
अतः भूयो अपि न इदानीम् इक्ष्वाकु पुर वासिनः |
स्वपेयुर् अनुरक्ता माम् वृष्क मूलानि संश्रिताः
verses.iast:
ataḥ bhūyo api na idānīm ikṣvāku pura vāsinaḥ |
svapeyur anuraktā mām vṛṣka mūlāni saṃśritāḥ
verses.translation: "From this the citizens of Ayodhya (the ancient capital of Ikshvaku), who are longing for me, may not sleep as of now, at the roots of trees again and again"

verses.devanagari:
पौरा हि आत्म कृतात् दुह्खात् विप्रमोच्या नृप आत्मजैः |
न तु खल्व् आत्मना योज्या दुह्खेन पुर वासिनः
verses.iast:
paurā hi ātma kṛtāt duhkhāt vipramocyā nṛpa ātmajaiḥ |
na tu khalv ātmanā yojyā duhkhena pura vāsinaḥ
verses.translation: "The residents of city should indeed be made free of their suffering brought about by (citizens) themselves, by the sons of their rulers. The citizens should on no account be burdened with hardship caused by (princes) them selves as is our case."

glosses.meaning: by the sons of their rulers. puravaasinaH = The citizens

verses.devanagari:
अब्रवील् लक्ष्मणो रामम् साक्षात् धर्मम् इव स्थितम् |
रोचते मे महा प्राज्ञ क्षिप्रम् आरुह्यताम् इति
verses.iast:
abravīl lakṣmaṇo rāmam sākṣāt dharmam iva sthitam |
rocate me mahā prāGYa kṣipram āruhyatām iti
verses.translation: Lakshmana replied as follows to Rama, who is standing firm like righteousness personified: "Oh, wise brother! What you say is agreeable to me. (Pray) ascend the chariot quickly"

glosses.meaning: thus. aaruhyataam = Let (the chariot) be mounted

verses.devanagari:
अथ रामोऽब्रवीच्छ्रीमान् सुमन्त्रम् युज्यताम् रथः |
गमिष्यामि ततोऽरण्यम् गच्छ श्रीघ्रमितः प्रभो
verses.iast:
atha rāmo'bravīcchrīmān sumantram yujyatām rathaḥ |
gamiśhyāmi tato'raṇyam gaccha śrīghramitaḥ prabho
verses.translation: Then, the glorious Rama spoke to the charioteer as follows: "Oh, capable man! Keep the chariot ready. I shall proceed to the forest. Let us go quickly from here."

verses.devanagari:
सूतः ततः सम्त्वरितः स्यन्दनम् तैः हय उत्तमैः |
योजयित्वा अथ रामाय प्रान्जलिः प्रत्यवेदयत्
verses.iast:
sūtaḥ tataḥ samtvaritaḥ syandanam taiḥ haya uttamaiḥ |
yojayitvā atha rāmāya prānjaliḥ pratyavedayat
verses.translation: Then, Sumantra quickly fastened the chariot to its excellent horses and thereafter submitted with joined palms to Rama (as follows):

verses.devanagari:
अयम् युक्तो महाबाहो रथस्ते रथिनाम् वर |
त्वमारोहस्व भद्रम् ते ससीतः सहलक्ष्मणः
verses.iast:
ayam yukto mahābāho rathaste rathinām vara |
tvamārohasva bhadram te sasītaḥ sahalakśmaṇaḥ
verses.translation: "Oh, mighty armed prince! Your chariot is kept ready. You ascend it along with Sita and with Lakshmana, Oh jewel among car-warriors! May prosperity attend you"

glosses.meaning: and with Lakshmana . bhadram = May prosperity be

verses.devanagari:
तम् स्यन्दनमधिष्ठाय राघवः सपरिच्छदः |
शीघ्रगामाकुलावर्ताम् तमसामतरन्नदीम्
verses.iast:
tam syandanamadhiśhṭhāya rāghavaḥ saparicchadaḥ |
śīghragāmākulāvartām tamasāmatarannadīm
verses.translation: Rama mounted the chariot with all necessaries (like bow, armor, quiver, spade, basket, and so on) and crossed the swift flowing Tamasa river, thickly set with whirl- pools.

verses.devanagari:
स सम्तीर्य महाबाहुः श्रीमान् शिवमकण्टकम् |
प्रापद्यत महामार्गमभयम् भयदर्शिनाम्
verses.iast:
sa samtīrya mahābāhuḥ śrīmān śivamakaṇṭakam |
prāpadyata mahāmārgamabhayam bhayadarśinām
verses.translation: Having duly crossed the stream, the glorious Rama the mighty armed reached a great road free from obstacles and safe even for those who are apprehensive of danger.

glosses.meaning: even for those who are apprehensive of danger.

verses.devanagari:
मोहन अर्थम् तु पौराणाम् सूतम् रामः अब्रवीद् वचः |
उदन् मुखः प्रयाहि त्वम् रथम् आस्थाय सारथे
मुहूर्तम् त्वरितम् गत्वा निर्गतय रथम् पुनः |
यथा न विद्युः पौरा माम् तथा कुरु समाहितः
verses.iast:
mohana artham tu paurāṇām sūtam rāmaḥ abravīd vacaḥ |
udan mukhaḥ prayāhi tvam ratham āsthāya sārathe
muhūrtam tvaritam gatvā nirgataya ratham punaḥ |
yathā na vidyuḥ paurā mām tathā kuru samāhitaḥ
verses.translation: In order to elude the citizens, Rama spoke to Sumantra as follows: "Oh, charioteer! You mount the chariot and go northward. Proceed for a while quickly and bring back the chariot again. Remaining careful, do it in such a way that the citizens may not be able to locate me"
notes: Comment:- How can Rama elude the citizens, who came off leaving their homes, showing their immense affection towards him? Love without self-centeredness knows what love is. Then the seemingly untruth is not untruth, the hurt in appearance is not really a hurt and the said deception is not a deception. Rama the knower of love was free to do what was right and whatever he did was righteous.

verses.devanagari:
रामस्य वचनम् श्रुत्वा तथा चक्रे स सारथिः |
प्रत्यागम्य च रामस्य स्यन्दनम् प्रत्यवेदयत्
verses.iast:
rāmasya vacanam śrutvā tathā cakre sa sārathiḥ |
pratyāgamya ca rāmasya syandanam pratyavedayat
verses.translation: Hearing Rama's advice, the charioteer made a round of the chariot as he was suggested and on returning, reported to Rama about the arrival of the chariot.

glosses.meaning: about the arrival of the chariot.

verses.devanagari:
तौ सम्प्रयुक्तम् तु रथम् समासित्थौ |
तदा ससीतौ रघवंशवर्धनौ |
प्रचोदयामास ततस्तुरम्गमान् |
स सारथिर्येन पथा तपोवनम्
verses.iast:
tau samprayuktam tu ratham samāsitthau |
tadā sasītau raghavaṃśavardhanau |
pracodayāmāsa tatasturamgamān |
sa sārathiryena pathā tapovanam
verses.translation: Then, Rama and Lakshmana(the promoters of the race of Raghu) along with Sita ascended the chariot yoked together. The charioteer urged the horses along the route by which they can reach a grove suited to the practice of austerities.

glosses.meaning: they can reach a grove suited to the practice of austerities.

verses.devanagari:
ततः समास्थाय रथम् महारथः
ससारथिर्धाशरथिर्वनम् ययौ |
उदङ्मुखम् तम् तु रथम् चकार स |
प्रयाणमाङ्गश्यनिवितदर्शनात्
verses.iast:
tataḥ samāsthāya ratham mahārathaḥ
sasārathirdhāśarathirvanam yayau |
udaṇ^mukham tam tu ratham cakāra sa |
prayāṇamāṇ^gaśyanivitadarśanāt
verses.translation: However, Sumantra placed that chariot by facing it to the north, for he saw omens auspicious for journey (in that quarter). Rama (son of Dasaratha) the mighty car-warrior, along with the charioteer mounted the chariot and proceeded to the forest.

glosses.meaning: for he saw omens auspicious for journey (in that quarter). DasharathiH = Rama (son of Dasaratha)
